title: Constructible preservation before biduality
statement: Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with structure morphism $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Work in the ordinary derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ for its bounded constructible complexes [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] having Tor amplitude in some finite interval [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Let $a_X^{\times}$ be the ambient right adjoint to ordinary etale compact-support direct image $Ra_{X!}$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], put $\omega_X=a_X^{\times}A$, and write $D_X=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\omega_X)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then $D_X$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ into itself. More precisely, for $d\in\mathbf N$, integers $a,b$, and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ with $\dim X\leq d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, the complex $D_XK$ has Tor amplitude in $[-b-2d,-a]$. This bound is independent of $n$.

proof.text: For the specified finite coefficient stage, prove that ell^n annihilates A: ell belongs to the maximal ideal of the coefficient integer ring because its spectral absolute value is less than one, and the chosen uniformizer generates that ideal. Its nth power belongs to the defining quotient ideal. Lift the equality to ULift using down_injective. The finite-field cardinality determines characteristic p on k_0 and hence on k; ell != p makes ell^n invertible on Spec k. This is the proved private helper coefficient_invertibleExponent. Finiteness is supplied by finite_coefficientExtensionRing.

The proved private equivalence boundedConstructible_iff converts the recorded bounded-constructibility predicate into the source library predicate. Apply the finite-constant-value versus finite-stalk constructibility comparison to each cohomology sheaf. Convert vanishing below and above bounds with DerivedCategory.isGE_iff and isLE_iff; in the reverse direction replace the lower bound a by min a b to ensure the required ordered interval. Convert hasTorAmplitudeIn to torAmplitudeIn using the existing proved hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_torAmplitudeIn equivalence, which tests the same tensor products.

Specialize the existing proved source-library implementation of this very node, AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.constructibleFiniteTor_and_torAmplitudeIn_verdierDual_of_perfectField, to the lifted coefficient ring and the structure morphism of X. The algebraic closure k is perfect; the geometric hypotheses and the given dimension inequality are exactly those of this theorem. Its Verdier dual unfolds to the specified derivedHom into finiteStageDualizingComplex, whose construction is unchanged. Convert its bounded-constructibility and Tor conclusions back with the equivalences of step 2. This reuses an existing implementation of the node, not a new statement or a self-import; the source proof uses smooth generic perfectness, stratum duality, direct-image bounds and Noetherian induction. No additional hypothesis, such as a <= b, is introduced.

For the qualitative clause, use exists_topologicalKrullDim_le for the finite-type structure morphism to obtain a natural d bounding dimension, and extract a,b from the input finite Tor condition. Apply the quantitative clause and existentially package its interval [-b-2d,-a]. The same arguments cover the empty scheme and empty Tor intervals; the displayed endpoints are independent of the coefficient level.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X$ be separated of finite type over $k$.
Its ambient dualizing object is $\omega_X=Ra_X^{\times}A$.
Write $D_X=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\omega_X)$.
Then $D_X$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$ into itself.
More precisely, if $\dim X\leq d$ and $K$ has Tor amplitude
in $[a,b]$, then $D_XK$ has Tor amplitude in
$[-b-2d,-a]$. This bound is independent of the exponent $n$.

proof.text:
Choose a finite stratification of $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ by smooth
locally closed subschemes $s:S\hookrightarrow X$ on which the
cohomology of $K$ is finite locally constant. Such a stratification
exists by constructibility, Noetherian induction, and the fact that a
reduced scheme over the perfect field $k$ has a dense smooth open in
each irreducible component. Nilpotent thickenings leave the etale site
unchanged. The finite-Tor restriction $P=s^*K$ is site-perfect:
successive local finite-free presentations give a bounded-above free
resolution, and truncation below the Tor bound leaves a finitely
presented flat last syzygy. This is the sheaf-local argument of
[lem-weil-bounded-finite-tor-perfect], with the notion of
[def-weil-site-perfect-complex]; it does not claim that each
cohomology module separately has finite projective dimension.

The open–closed triangles of
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement] build $K$, by finitely many
cones, from the objects $Rs_!P$. Ambient tensor adjunction gives

$$
D_XRs_!P\cong
Rs_*R\mathcal Hom_A(P,Rs^{\times}\omega_X)
=Rs_*D_SP.
$$

This is [lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom] for the locally closed
immersion, using composition of right adjoints. It is an ambient
identity, so it assumes no constructible preservation by $D_X$.
On a stratum of dimension $r$, the ambient smooth theorem
[thm-asd-smooth-tensor] makes $\omega_S$ an invertible sheaf
shifted by $[2r]$. Thus $D_SP=P^\vee\otimes\omega_S$ is
a site-perfect complex of Tor amplitude
$[-b-2r,-a-2r]$. The direct-image
theorem [thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude], with the uniform
vanishing bound of [lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing], makes
$Rs_*D_SP$ bounded constructible of Tor amplitude
$[-b-2r,-a]$, contained in $[-b-2d,-a]$.
The localization triangles assemble these pieces by extensions;
tensoring such a triangle with any module sheaf preserves the common
vanishing interval. Exactness of internal Hom in its first variable
therefore gives the stated bound for $D_XK$. Taking $K=A_X$ also proves that
$\omega_X$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude.
